name: law_firm_software_021_invoice_aging_dispute_risk_report
instruction: Build the firm's AR aging and dispute-risk report for this episode, batched under the episode batch code (ops_meta, meta_key='episode_state'; the episode row also carries the episode date and the dispute_risk_threshold knob the risk flag is cut by). Apply the firm's open-AR definition in firm policy KPI-CLIENT-01 exactly as the live policy row states it — including how invoices in dispute interact with the aging (they are aged like any other open invoice AND separately risk-flagged when their unpaid balance clears the episode row's threshold). Age the open invoices the way the policy and standard practice prescribe and push one ops_reports row per non-empty bucket (report='ar_aging', batch_code) carrying the bucket, its invoice count and its unpaid total; push one ops_reports row per risk-flagged invoice (report='dispute_risk', batch_code) identifying the invoice and its unpaid balance. STAGE 2 — firm policy SEVERITY-01 requires a report that summarizes another to reuse the summarized rows' values rather than recompute them: from the bucket rows, push exactly one ops_reports row (report='ar_concentration', batch_code) carrying the share of open AR sitting past 90 days. STAGE 3 — the firm's close calendar also defines six standard month-end close dates relative to the episode month (the six calendar month-ends immediately preceding it); reconstruct the aging as of each of those close dates on the same open-invoice basis the policy defines, counting only invoices that had been issued by that date, and push one ops_reports row per non-empty bucket per close date (report='ar_aging_history', batch_code). No other ops_reports rows for these reports and this batch may exist. Every collection this task doesn't write to must remain untouched.

hazards.mechanism: The disputed-in-aging interaction: disputed invoices are part of open AR under policy KPI-CLIENT-01, so they age inside their due-date bucket AND get risk-flagged when their unpaid balance exceeds the episode threshold. Excluding them from the aging shifts ~449 invoices' balances across buckets (snapshot-confirmed: 449 disputed invoices with positive unpaid balance); flagging the ones under the threshold over-reports the risk set (snapshot unpaid balances run ~536-14,995, so the 2000-8000 knob moves the flag set between 403/312/212).

The 'current' bucket legitimately includes open invoices not yet past due at the episode date (snapshot: 107), and the 90+ concentration must be dollar-weighted (unpaid totals, not invoice counts) — a count-based concentration is plausible and wrong.

success_criteria.summary: Every aging bucket's count and unpaid total independently confirmed via raw-row bucketing AND a SQL date-arithmetic GROUP BY, agreeing with each other and with the written rows; every dispute_risk row matches a real disputed invoice above the episode threshold and none below it; the concentration percentage derived by read-back from the bucket rows; the six month-end reconstructions exact including interior-month exclusion.

checks.expect: one ar_aging row per non-empty bucket, one dispute_risk row per qualifying invoice, one ar_concentration row, ar_aging_history rows per non-empty bucket per close date
bucket membership and totals agree between Python bucketing and SQL date arithmetic
excluding disputed invoices from the aging, flagging sub-threshold disputes, or computing concentration from counts => FAIL

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Fuses standard AR aging bucketing, a policy-defined disputed-in-aging interaction, an episode-knob dispute-risk flag, and a six-month-end point-in-time reconstruction in one mission at 3000-invoice scale — distinct from 015's client-centric rollup (which carries the quarter-end variant) and 019's aggregate-only disruption buckets.
